sentences.text: Georgiasaurus was a large polycotylid plesiosaur that measured between 4 and 5 meters in length.
Paleontologist Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of this animal at 450 kg.
The genus Georgiasaurus was described by Otschev in 1977.
The name Georgiasaurus means "Georgy's lizard" and honors the author's father, Georgy Otschev, who died before the 1976 publication.
The holotype specimen POKM 11658 originally contained a complete skeleton but was damaged during quarry stone preparation.
The fossil remains were discovered near the village of Zatolokino.
Georgiasaurus belongs to the subfamily Polycotylinae.
The genus Georgiasaurus is classified within the family Polycotylidae.
Georgiasaurus lived during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
